name: Question 12
problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨2t-3,\,3{t}^{2}-6t+2⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $r=⟨2,\,0⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the times when the particle is at the origin. Do not round the answers.

In **ascending order**, the particle is at the origin when $t=$
{{field-1}}
and $t=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
The particle is at the origin when its position is $r=⟨0,0⟩.$ So first, we need to compute the position function of the particle.

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨2t-3,\,3{t}^{2}-6t+2⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int (2t-3)\,\text{d}t,\,\int (3{t}^{2}-6t+2)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{2}-3t+{C}_{1},\,{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨2,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨0-0+{C}_{1},\,0-0+0+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨2,0⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=2$ and ${C}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨{t}^{2}-3t+2,\,{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the times at which the particle is at the origin, we solve the equation $r(t)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{t}^{2}-3t+2,\,{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-3t+2 & =(t-1)(t-2)=0\,⇒\,t=1,2, \\ {t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t & =t(t-1)(t-2)=0\,⇒\,t=0,1,2.\end{aligned}
$$

The values of $t$ that satisfy both equations are $t=1$ and $t=2.$ 

Therefore, in ascending order, the particle is at the origin when
$t=1$ and $t=2.$

EXPLANATION

The particle is at the origin when its position is r=⟨0,0⟩. So first, we need to compute the position function of the particle.

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector: r(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫⟨2t−3,3t2−6t+2⟩dt=⟨∫(2t−3)dt,∫(3t2−6t+2)dt⟩=⟨t2−3t+C1,t3−3t2+2t+C2⟩.

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that r(0)=⟨2,0⟩. Substituting t=0, we get r(0)=⟨0−0+C1,0−0+0+C2⟩⟨2,0⟩=⟨C1,C2⟩, so we must have C1=2 and C2=0. Therefore, the position of P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨t2−3t+2,t3−3t2+2t⟩.

To find the times at which the particle is at the origin, we solve the equation r(t)=0: ⟨t2−3t+2,t3−3t2+2t⟩=⟨0,0⟩.

So we need t2−3t+2=(t−1)(t−2)=0⇒t=1,2,t3−3t2+2t=t(t−1)(t−2)=0⇒t=0,1,2.

The values of t that satisfy both equations are t=1 and t=2.

Therefore, in ascending order, the particle is at the origin when t=1 and t=2.
